images.caption: Figure 1:Test-TimeBaking (TTB) is a feed-forward, generalizable view synthesis model that bakes scene information from cross-view attention into a fast-weight MLP, achieving constant-complexity rendering with quality on par with decoder-only architectures. TTB sits on the Pareto frontier of PSNR vs. FPS, rendering up to23×23\timesfaster than cross-attention baseline at comparable quality.

Figure 2:Motivation.We show three variants of the inner-loop optimization in TTT-style fast-weight MLPs.(a)TTT with KV binding[77]learns from raw value tokens projected fromX(ctx)X^{(\text{ctx})}.(b)TTB without context pairing targets the cross-view attention output instead, collaborating with attention rather than replacing it.(c)Our full TTB additionally pairs each context view:X(ctx-gt)X^{(\text{ctx-gt})}carries image content and supplies the cross-view attended target, whileX(ctx-rend)X^{(\text{ctx-rend})}is camera-only and matches the modality ofX(nv)X^{(\text{nv})}. The t-SNE plots show that only (c) aligns the modalities from the first block.

Figure 3:Pipeline.Our model stacksLLidentical blocks of Intra-view Attention, FFN, Test-Time Baking, and FFN. In the reconstruction stage, each context view is duplicated into a context pair, where the context ground-truth tokenX(ctx-gt)X^{(\text{ctx-gt})}carries RGB and pose while the context rendering tokenX(ctx-rend)X^{(\text{ctx-rend})}is pose-only and matches the modality of the novel rendering tokenX(nv)X^{(\text{nv})}. At each TTB layer, the inner-loopupdatebakes the fast-weight MLP via MSE loss to mapX(ctx-rend)X^{(\text{ctx-rend})}toward the cross-view attention output ofX(ctx-gt)X^{(\text{ctx-gt})}.
The baked MLP isappliedto serve three token streams: it propagates bothX(ctx-rend)X^{(\text{ctx-rend})}andX(nv)X^{(\text{nv})}to the next layer, and provides feedback toX(ctx-gt)X^{(\text{ctx-gt})}as an auxiliary signal. In the novel-view rendering stage, each token retrieves global scene information inO⁡(1)O(1)from the baked MLP, instead ofO⁡(N)O(N)via cross-attention. The rendering loss is backpropagated through the inner-loop baking process to train the model end-to-end.
Figure 5:Qualitative comparison on DL3DV.TTB preserves fine details on par with DVSM[58], while LaCT[77]and LVSM[25]produce visible blur.
Figure 6:Qualitative comparison on in-the-wild datasets.TTB generalizes to out-of-domain scenes and preserves fine details consistent with the in-domain results.
